repo_notes.content:
NeuroWatch is an open-source (Apache-2.0) video recorder (NVR) for IP cameras on Linux and Windows: a Rust recorder service, a Python/PySide6 desktop app, and analytics plugins that run as separate processes.

docs/technical/ is the authoritative description of the architecture. It is generated from the canonical pages at https://neurowatch.app/docs (never edited by hand); prefer it to older notes elsewhere in docs/, and keep its anchor ids when linking.

Key directories: crates/nw-backend (the recorder service: streams/, pipeline/, recording/, playback/, export/, events/, onvif_events/, plugin_host/, shm/, ipc/, cloud/); crates/nw-core (shared types); crates/nw-analytics-protocol and crates/nw-analytics-sdk (the plugin protocol and Rust SDK); sdk/python (the Python plugin SDK); ui/neurowatch (the desktop app, tray and service controller).

The free plugins, NeuroWatch Motion and NeuroWatch Detect, live in their own public repositories. Do not quote benchmark figures or describe the video path as copy-free: the docs deliberately make neither claim.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: How the NeuroWatch camera recorder is built: a Rust recorder service, a Qt desktop app and analytics plugins as separate processes, and the rules behind them. Follow docs/technical/overview.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs) and the code it names.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Inside the NeuroWatch recorder service and an analytics plugin: the modules, who owns which thread, how the service starts and how it restarts itself. Follow docs/technical/architecture.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/architecture) and the code it names.

pages.title: Stream engine and buffers
pages.purpose: How NeuroWatch opens each camera stream once, numbers every picture, caches the current GOP and gives each reader a bounded queue with its own loss rule. Follow docs/technical/stream-engine.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/stream-engine) and the code it names.

pages.title: Decoding and hardware acceleration
pages.purpose: When NeuroWatch decodes video, how it ranks VA-API, NVDEC, Direct3D, Quick Sync and V4L2 decoders, and how it falls back to the CPU without losing the camera. Follow docs/technical/hardware-decoding.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/hardware-decoding) and the code it names.

pages.title: Desktop rendering
pages.purpose: How pictures reach the NeuroWatch video wall: shared-memory rings, NV12 converted on the GPU, a reader that sets its rate, and latest-frame-only painting. Follow docs/technical/desktop-rendering.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/desktop-rendering) and the code it names.

pages.title: Recording, playback and export
pages.purpose: How NeuroWatch records cameras as segmented Matroska without decoding, indexes them in SQLite, protects missing drives, archives to a NAS and exports MP4 clips. Follow docs/technical/recording.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/recording) and the code it names.

pages.title: Browser viewing
pages.purpose: What the NeuroWatch recorder does for browser viewers: the camera's own H.264 or H.265 passed through, a fast start from the GOP cache, and when it converts. Follow docs/technical/browser-viewing.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/browser-viewing) and the code it names.

pages.title: Analytics plugins
pages.purpose: How NeuroWatch analytics plugins work: separate processes over sockets, TLS or QUIC, signed keys, compressed or shared pictures, drawings tied to pictures. Follow docs/technical/plugins.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/plugins) and the code it names.

pages.title: Events and integrations
pages.purpose: How NeuroWatch handles events: an EventHub that never waits on the database, ONVIF push and pull, plugin events, pictures, alerts and MQTT. Follow docs/technical/events.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/events) and the code it names.

pages.title: Engineering in Rust
pages.purpose: Why the NeuroWatch recorder is written in Rust, the rules its code follows for locks, errors and streaming threads, how it is tested, and its licence. Follow docs/technical/rust.md (from https://neurowatch.app/docs/rust) and the code it names.
